Plot a prediction: one map per day

Source: R/plots.R
plot.bruce_prediction.Rd

One small map per day. With scale = "common" all days share one colour scale, so days can be compared directly (from the 0.5% to the 99.5% quantile of all days, so a few extreme cells do not wash out the rest). With scale = "free" each day gets its own scale and legend, which shows the pattern within the city on every day, even on days much cooler or warmer than the rest. With scale = "anomaly" each day is shown minus its own city mean, on one symmetric scale: how much hotter or cooler each place is than the city that day, comparable across days.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bruce_prediction'
plot(
  x,
  what = c("mean", "sd"),
  scale = c("common", "free", "anomaly"),
  dates = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A bruce_prediction.

what

"mean" (default) or "sd" (uncertainty; needs a prediction made with n_samples > 0).

scale

"common" (default), "free" or "anomaly" (see Details; "anomaly" only for what = "mean").

dates

Days to plot (default: all).

ncol

Maps per row (default: up to 6).

main

Overall title.

...

Unused.
